council_controls: Clearing fly-tipping seen on a road, pavement or public space in Southampton, handled as a street cleaning problem. Council aims to deal with at least 75% of urgent requests within one working day. The council also has a page on fixed penalty notices for fly-tipping.
out_of_scope: Fly-tipping on private land or property: owner or occupier must resolve it (council page, checked 2026-10-17).
not_confirmed_or_to_check: Builders/landlords duty of care covered in info_student_waste_rules.
evidence_seen: Council environmental issues page (street cleaning section) and street cleaning menu.

council_controls: Dead animals seen on a road, pavement or public space, reported as a street cleaning problem.
out_of_scope: Private land: owner/occupier responsible, contact a vet (council page, 2026-10-17).
evidence_seen: Council environmental issues page (street cleaning section).

council_controls: Street cleaning problems on a road, pavement or public space. The council has local street cleansing teams and a separate commercial street cleansing service.

not_confirmed_or_to_check: Resolved 2026-10-17: trolleys go to the retailer first; leaves cleared Oct to mid-Jan, reports only for serious hazard or flood risk.

evidence_seen: Council environmental issues page (street cleaning section).

category: Broken glass / spillage / dangerous item on the street
council_controls: Spillages, broken glass and other dangerous items seen on a road, pavement or public space, reported as a street cleaning problem.
out_of_scope: Not stated: large fuel or chemical spills. Our own rule is to show emergency guidance first for anything dangerous.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: Ask how the council handles oil or fuel spills and whether another body deals with them.
evidence_seen: Council environmental issues page (street cleaning section).

council_controls: Potholes on roads the council maintains. The council reports repairing 5,204 potholes in the last 12 months and spending over 1.4 million pounds on dedicated pothole repair. Much of the road repair work is delivered with its highways partner, Balfour Beatty Living Places.
out_of_scope: Motorways and trunk roads belong to National Highways. This is stated on other councils' pages, not on Southampton's own page.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: Private roads are not verified. Check response times and how the council classifies urgent potholes.
evidence_seen: Council environmental issues page and council news article on the highways and footways programme.

council_controls: Abandoned vehicles can be reported to the council through its roads and parking options.
out_of_scope: Not investigated if legally parked with no signs of abandonment, only a nuisance because of where parked, or on private land with permission.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: Resolved 2026-10-17 from council page (criteria, DVLA contact-details rule, 4-8 weeks untaxed).
evidence_seen: Council environmental issues page (roads and parking section).

council_controls: Noise from a neighbouring property. The council has a neighbourhood nuisance page and a noise complaint form.
out_of_scope: Not stated: noise from businesses or licensed premises, and road traffic noise. Threats or violence are for the police (999). That is our safety rule, not a council statement.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: Resolved 2026-10-17: council excluded-noise list read in full (see scope_checks.csv).
evidence_seen: Council environmental issues page and council environment menu.

category: Light, dust, smoke or odour from a neighbouring property

category: Concern about a property (very dirty, hoarding, possible rodents)
council_controls: Properties that have become very dirty, with possible rodent infestations, or where hoarded possessions make access difficult. The council investigates these concerns.
out_of_scope: Not stated: general untidy gardens or minor upkeep issues.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: Check what the council does after investigating and who it can enter or order to clean.

council_controls: Missed household collections. Residents should report within two working days of the original collection day. The council aims to return within two to five working days. The form shows what the collection crew logged.
out_of_scope: Not counted as missed: wrong bin put out, contaminated bin, bin not visible to the crew, bins not supplied by the council, items the council cannot collect (such as rubble or clinical waste), or reports made after the window.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: The council has published a notice about ongoing collection disruption. The page is undated, so re-check before the demo.
evidence_seen: Council missed bin collection page and Leader's waste update.

council_controls: Lost, damaged or stray bins. Homes with storage get a green-top general waste bin, a blue-top recycling bin and a black or grey glass box. Homes without storage get rolls of sacks, delivered twice a year and requestable.
out_of_scope: The council asks residents to check first whether the bin was moved, claimed by a neighbour or returned to the wrong property.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: Charges for replacement bins were not checked.
evidence_seen: Council lost, damaged or stray bins page.

category: Repair for a council tenant or leaseholder
council_controls: Repairs for council tenants and leaseholders, through a dedicated online form.
out_of_scope: Private landlords, housing associations and letting agents are not covered by this form. Private rented homes go to Private Sector Housing (see the partly confirmed file).
not_confirmed_or_to_check: The urgent and out-of-hours repair route was not checked.

category: Student question: who deals with bins and rubbish at my house
council_controls: Council guidance says tenants, not landlords, are responsible for household waste. Everyone in the house shares responsibility for correct bins, putting them out and bringing them back in. Repeatedly leaving bins on the street can lead to a 60 pound fine. The council collects domestic rubbish and recycling put out for collection.
out_of_scope: Bulky items and building rubbish are not part of normal collection. A chargeable bulky waste service exists for residential households. A council landlord leaflet says landlords are responsible for waste from building work they commission.
not_confirmed_or_to_check: The bulky and landlord points come from a council leaflet and a Solent University student PDF, not the main student page. Re-check them and the fine amount on the council site before the demo.
evidence_seen: Council information for students about household waste page, plus council landlord leaflet.
